Summary of Changes
------------------

**Major Changes:**
* docs/clustermesh: overhaul Cluster Mesh documentation with a new introduction, improved load-balancing guidance, and Helm-first setup and certificate configuration instructions (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47615, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47351, @MrFreezeex)

**Minor Changes:**
* envoy: demote stale ADS endpoint warning (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47148, @nezdolik)
* Speed up recovery time for disrupted TCP connections that access a DSR-enabled Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47529, @julianwiedmann)

**Bugfixes:**
* azure: Stop issuing redundant CiliumNode status updates on every IPAM sync when the node's Azure interfaces are unchanged. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47449, @jaredledvina)
* bpf: dsr: don't look for TCP header on fragmented packets (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47640, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: hostfw: tolerate unknown CT protocols and rely on policies (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47621, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47343, @smagnani96)
* clustermesh: fix MCS-API CRD install/upgrade when clustermesh-apiserver is started before the CRD version is actually installed (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47824, @MrFreezeex)
* datapath: turn ARP off on the base devices before bringing them up (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47838, @aanm)
* endpoint/watchdog: Avoid warning about endpoints being deleted (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47625, @christarazi)
* endpoint: Fix silent CIDR policy bypass and traffic drops after agent restart (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47880, @weizhoublue)
* envoy.httpUpstreamLingerTimeout accepts `0` as a chart value and templates into configmap. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47741, @jdw6359)
* envoy: restore http-idle-timeout as the route idle timeout source (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47583, @aanm)
* Fix a BPF verifier reject on pre-v5.12 kernels, when IPv6 is enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47765, @julianwiedmann)
* Fix a deadlock in the shutdown of Cilium operator related to CiliumEndpointSlices. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47967, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47802, @bimmlerd)
* Fix a NetworkPolicy update being ignored for up to two minutes when it arrived while an endpoint was waiting for its security identity to be resolved after a pod relabel. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47727, @aanm)
* Fix a spurious "unable to find ifindex for interface MAC" agent warning on EKS ENI IPAM by waiting for the ENI netlink interface before configuring ingress routes and rules. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47295, @aanm)
* Fix abnormal ip allocation caused by hostnetwork pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47552, @haozhangami)
* Fix unintended RevDNAT for client-to-pod TCP connections, when an identical connection was previously established through a DSR Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47593, @julianwiedmann)
* fix: allow setting endpointPolicyUpdateTimeoutDuration in helm (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47754, @weizhoublue)
* Fixed an issue where an HTTPRoute referencing a Gateway with mixed listener protocols (e.g. HTTP and TCP) was incorrectly rejected with `NotAllowedByListeners` when the TCP listener had an explicit `AllowedRoutes.Kinds` restriction. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46842, @pidreher)
* gateway-api/gamma: refresh CEC owner refs on route recreation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47840, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: mark unresolved backend service ports in route status (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47766, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: preserve duplicate HTTPRoute rule precedence (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46696, @thorn3r)
* gateway-api: prevent conflicted listeners from reaching ingestion (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47457, @asauber)
* gateway-api: requeue L4/TLS routes on ServiceImport updates (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47702, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: sync ListenerSet TLS secrets on ListenerSet events (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47627, @mhofstetter)
* ipcache: fix CIDR reference counter to use canonical prefixes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47208, @iwanhae)
* l2announcer: re-evaluate services on frontend changes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47579, @mhofstetter)
* Log the correct route kind when the Gateway API operator fails to list TLSRoutes for a backend Service (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47826, @mehrdadbn9)
* operator: Emit startup logs in the configured log format (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47890, @HadrienPatte)
* Resolve a endpoint manager crash for restored endpoints with verbose policy logging enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47844, @bimmlerd)
* standalone-dns-proxy: return an error when no endpoint is found (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47791, @vipul-21)
* wireguard: Unsubscribe node handler on shutdown (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47614, @HadrienPatte)

signals.title: CFP: BFD(Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) support in BGP Control plane
signals.text: ## BFD(Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) support in BGP Control plane BFD is a health checking mechanism made for rapid (sub second) failure detection of data forwarding planes. Its a protocol which can be employed together with protocols such as BGP, IS-IS and OSFP to shorten the time between a failure and automated actions like retracting routes to reroute traffic. The protocol is describes in [RFC5880](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5880) with the addition of [RFC5881](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5881) for single hop and [RFC5882](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5882) for multi hop monitoring. Adding this feature to our BGP Control Plane would allow users with peers that also support the protocol to reduce downtime in case of failures in Cilium or between Cilium and peers. ## Implementation proposal Currently our only BGP backend is GoBGP which as of writing this has no BFD support. So we will have to implement it one way or another. ### GoBGP native The first logical approach would be to add it to GoBGP directly via a PR. GoBGP maintainers have already [indicated](https://github.com/osrg/gobgp/issues/2563) that they are open to PRs for this feature. Once BFD support is merged upstream and we are able to update to a GoBGP version with BFD support we will have to plumb access to it from our CRD. ### Cilium native The second approach would be to add BFD capabilities to Cilium directly, either in the agent or the datapath or a combination of the two. BFD works for any application where forwarding takes place such as the Cilium datapath. Having a non-BGP specific implementation would allow us to also use the protocol internally to monitor inter-node connections and connections in standalone L4LB for upstream and downstream. BFD control packets are sent over UDP in small packets (for IPv4/IPv6 single and multi hop) which is easily parse-able in both XDP and TC layers. The largest obstacle to a pure eBPF based implementation would be the need to send packets on a timer. However, if the peer is in Demand mode we only have to answer to Poll messages and optionally send echo messages back both of which are request-reply without delay. In this case, we should manually set associated BGP sessions to AdminDown in case of a BFD failure. ### CRD plubing No matter which route we take for BFD implementation, we will have to provide our users with a way to configure it. Since BGP Control Plane is backend agnostic and not all backends might implement BFD in future, I suggest adding a annotation for the top level CRD. Something like `io.cilium/bfd: "enabled=true,active=true,echo=false,detect-multiplied=5,receive-interval=40000,transmit-interval=20000"` ### User feedback Any information we have regrading BFD sessions should be added to the agent output (#22009). BFD adds additional diagnostic codes to communicate why a session is down which might be useful in figuring out what is going on. We should also add BFD specific information to the peer information to show the received discriminator and timing values. ### Metrics As soon as we have BFD session information, it should be added to the BGP metrics described in (#22010)

signals.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signals.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. When migrating variables, do a quick search through [Paul's macro documentation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/15379#issuecomment-897441189) for a good docstring to use in `DECLARE_CONFIG`. - [ep_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/ep_config.h) - [x] HOST_EP_ID - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [node_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/node_config.h) - [x] CLUSTER_ID - [x] CILIUM_*_IFINDEX, CILIUM_*_MAC (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43474) - [x] TUNNEL_PORT, TUNNEL_PROTOCOL (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43520) - [x] KERNEL_HZ, ENABLE_JIFFIES (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] L2_ANNOUNCEMENTS(_MAX_LIVENESS) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42587) - [x] EPHEMERAL_MIN (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43564) - [x] IS_L3_DEV, NATIVE_DEV_MAC_BY_IFINDEX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/39116 & https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] CLUSTER_ID_MAX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42478) - [x] IDENTITY_{LEN,MAX} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43507) - [x] VTEP_MASK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] NODEPORT_PORT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] IPV4_LOOPBACK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [x] NAT_46X64_PREFIX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43799) - [x] CIDR_IDENTITY_RANGE_{START,END} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44223) - [x] HASH_INIT{4,6}_SEED (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44190) - [x] EVENTS_MAP_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44795) - [ ] VLAN_FILTER (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38721) - [x] Reserved security IDs (HOST_ID, WORLD_ID, ect.) signals.title: CFP: Network Quality of Service (QOS) API
signals.text: ## Cilium Feature Proposal **Is your proposed feature related to a problem?** Yes. Currently, Cilium's QoS implementation using bandwidth manager is a node-local solution (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/24194). It uses an internal priority field in the kernel (skb->priority) to order packets on the node, but this priority is not preserved in the packet header when it leaves the node. This means that downstream network devices like routers and switches are unaware of the packet's priority, and cannot provide end-to-end Quality of Service. **Describe the feature you'd like** We would like a declarative, Kubernetes-native way to apply QOS tagging to egress traffic from pods. This would allow administrators to define QoS policies that are respected across the entire network. **Declarative and Extensible API:** - The API must be Kubernetes-native and declarative. - It should be designed as a generic QoS framework that can be extended in the future to support mechanisms beyond DSCP, such as bandwidth shaping or other traffic control features. **Flexible Traffic Selection:** The mechanism for applying QoS policies must be flexible and support selection based on: - Workload: Kubernetes-native selectors for pods and namespaces (podSelector, namespaceSelector). - L4 Flow: Granular selection based on protocol (TCP/UDP), source port, and destination port. **Initial Use Case:** The initial implementation within this framework can focus on specific DSCP marking of egress packets. The system must allow specifying any DSCP value within the standard 0-63 range. The division and quantization of this range should be determined by Cluster Administrators, recognizing that many organizations operate complex network environments with established QoS policies that leverage the entire 0-63 DSCP range. Integration with Existing Features: - The new QoS framework should integrate with Cilium's existing features, such as the bandwidth manager and the current local traffic shaping implementation. https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/24194 **Notify relevant community channels** - @cilium/bandwidth-manager **(Optional) Describe your proposed solution** This solution outlines a persona-based approach to Quality of Service (QoS) in Cilium, designed to provide a flexible and powerful way to manage network traffic prioritization. This model introduces a clear separation of concerns by defining three distinct personas, each with specific roles and responsibilities: Cluster Providers, Infrastructure Admins, and Application Developers. **The Personas** - Cluster Providers: Define the available QoS mechanisms (e.g., DSCP, NodePriority) using the QoSMechanism CRD. - Infrastructure Admins: Create reusable QoS profiles (e.g., "low-latency", "voice", "guaranteed") from the available mechanisms using the QoSClass CRD. - Application Developers: Apply the predefined QoS classes to their workloads using the QoSPolicy CRD. **Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)** The following example shows how DSCP as well as node priority can be defined and used under the new proposed model. Node priority refers to [CFP 24194](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/24194) **QoSMechanism (Cluster Provider)** Declares a supported QoS mechanism in the cluster. ```yaml # Declares that DSCP tagging is available. apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1 kind: QoSMechanism metadata: name: dscp spec: type: DSCP description: "Provides DSCP tagging for egress traffic." --- # Declares that NodePriority (node-local FQ scheduler prioritization) is available. apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1 kind: QoSMechanism metadata: name: node-priority spec: type: NodePriority description: "Provides node-local packet prioritization using FQ scheduler priority levels." ``` **QoSClass (Infrastructure Admin)** Defines a reusable QoS profile based on an available mechanism. ```yaml # Defines a "voice" class using the dscp mechanism. apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1 kind: QoSClass metadata: name: voice spec: priority: 100 # Higher number indicates higher precedence during policy collisions mechanismRef: name: dscp parameters: value: 46 # Expedited Forwarding (EF) --- # Defines a "guaranteed" class using the node-priority mechanism. Priority is strictly mechanism-local; it resolves conflicts only between classes sharing the same underlying mechanism (e.g., DSCP vs DSCP) and does not affect orthogonal mechanisms applied concurrently. apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1 kind: QoSClass metadata: name: guaranteed spec: priority: 90 mechanismRef: name: node-priority parameters: priority: Guaranteed ``` **QoSPolicy (Application Developer)** Applies one or more QoS classes to selected pods and egress traffic flows. ```yaml # Applies the "voice" DSCP QoS class and the "guaranteed" node-priority QoS class # to egress traffic destined for 192.168.1.0/24 on UDP port 5060 and TCP port 8080. apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1 kind: QoSPolicy metadata: name: payment-app-qos namespace: production spec: podSelector: matchLabels: app: payment-processor egress: - toCIDR: - 192.168.1.0/24 toPorts: - ports: - port: "5060" protocol: UDP - port: "8080" protocol: TCP qosClassRefs: - name: voice - name: guaranteed ``` ### Policy Collisions and Conflict Resolution When multiple `QoSPolicy` resources match the same pod and traffic flow, conflicts can arise if they assign different QoS classes for the same mechanism. Because mechanisms like DSCP do not have an inherent SLA hierarchy, conflicts are resolved using the following rules: - **Rule Specificity:** Granular L4 flow rules override broader L3 rules, and rules matching a more specific destination CIDR take precedence over broader CIDR matches. - **Class Priority Precedence:** When two independent policies have the exact same specificity but configure conflicting QoS classes for the same mechanism, Cilium evaluates the explicit `spec.priority` field defined on the `QoSClass` resources.

signals.title: BGP CRD's doesn't get created
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.5 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? I'm deploying Cilium on a one node Talos (v1.13.6) cluster. The cluster is dual stack, and Cilium is deployed through an inline manifest. The manifest gets created with the following `helm template` command: `helm template cilium cilium/cilium --version 1.19.5 --namespace kube-system --set ipam.mode=kubernetes --set kubeProxyReplacement=true --set securityContext.capabilities.ciliumAgent="{CHOWN,KILL,NET_ADMIN,NET_RAW,IPC_LOCK,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE,DAC_OVERRIDE,FOWNER,SETGID,SETUID,NET_BIND_SERVICE}" --set securityContext.capabilities.cleanCiliumState="{NET_ADMIN,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE}" --set cgroup.autoMount.enabled=false --set cgroup.hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup --set k8sServiceHost=apiserver.my.domain.tld --set k8sServicePort=6443 --set gatewayAPI.enabled=true --set ipv4.enabled=true --set ipv6.enabled=true --set hubble.relay.enabled=true --set authentication.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.install.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.install.server.dataStorage.enabled=false --set hubble.peerService.clusterDomain=k8s.my.domain.tld --set hubble.ui.enabled=true --set encryption.enabled=true --set encryption.type=wireguard --set encryption.nodeEncryption=true --set bgpControlPlane.enabled=true > .\cilium_template.yaml` After bringing up the cluster, I'm expecting cilium-operator to create the CRD's for Cilium BGP configuration, but they're missing: `kubectl api-resources --api-group=cilium.io NAME SHORTNAMES APIVERSION NAMESPACED KIND ciliumcidrgroups ccg cilium.io/v2 false CiliumCIDRGroup ciliumclusterwideenvoyconfigs ccec cilium.io/v2 false CiliumClusterwideEnvoyConfig ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies ccnp cilium.io/v2 false CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy ciliumendpoints cep,ciliumep cilium.io/v2 true CiliumEndpoint ciliumenvoyconfigs cec cilium.io/v2 true CiliumEnvoyConfig ciliumgatewayclassconfigs cgcc cilium.io/v2alpha1 true CiliumGatewayClassConfig ciliumidentities ciliumid cilium.io/v2 false CiliumIdentity ciliuml2announcementpolicies l2announcement cilium.io/v2alpha1 false CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy ciliumloadbalancerippools ippools,ippool,lbippool,lbippools cilium.io/v2 false CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool ciliumnetworkpolicies cnp,ciliumnp cilium.io/v2 true CiliumNetworkPolicy ciliumnodeconfigs cilium.io/v2 true CiliumNodeConfig ciliumnodes cn,ciliumn cilium.io/v2 false CiliumNode ciliumpodippools cpip cilium.io/v2alpha1 false CiliumPodIPPool` `cilium bgp peers` returns the following error message: `Error: Unable to get peering status: failed to unmarshal bgp state from cilium-v5b8v: invalid character 'B' looking for beginning of value` ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Install Talos v.1.13.6 without Kubeprism and with an inline manifest created by the following command: `helm template cilium cilium/cilium --version 1.19.5 --namespace kube-system --set ipam.mode=kubernetes --set kubeProxyReplacement=true --set securityContext.capabilities.ciliumAgent="{CHOWN,KILL,NET_ADMIN,NET_RAW,IPC_LOCK,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE,DAC_OVERRIDE,FOWNER,SETGID,SETUID,NET_BIND_SERVICE}" --set securityContext.capabilities.cleanCiliumState="{NET_ADMIN,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE}" --set cgroup.autoMount.enabled=false --set cgroup.hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup --set k8sServiceHost=apiserver.my.domain.tld --set k8sServicePort=6443 --set gatewayAPI.enabled=true --set ipv4.enabled=true --set ipv6.enabled=true --set hubble.relay.enabled=true --set authentication.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.install.enabled=true --set authentication.mutual.spire.install.server.dataStorage.enabled=false --set hubble.peerService.clusterDomain=k8s.my.domain.tld --set hubble.ui.enabled=true --set encryption.enabled=true --set encryption.type=wireguard --set encryption.nodeEncryption=true --set bgpControlPlane.enabled=true` 2. Run `kubectl api-resources --api-group=cilium.io`. The CRD's for BGP management will not be there. ### Cilium Version cilium-cli: v0.19.5 compiled with go1.26.4 on windows/amd64 cilium image (default): v1.19.4 cilium image (stable): v1.19.5 cilium image (running): unknown. Unable to obtain cilium version. signals.title: Host datapath BPF programs leak on every device change, exhausting kernel executable memory
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? A bonded interface on the node was being torn down and recreated every ~34s (unrelated host misconfiguration). The bond carries three VLAN sub-interfaces, so each cycle removes and re-adds three managed devices, producing two host-datapath reloads: ```bash 11:17:04 msg="Devices changed" devices="[eno1 interconnect]" 11:17:05 msg="Devices changed" devices="[public.3212 public.3211 eno1 interconnect public.1537]" 11:17:37 msg="Devices changed" devices="[eno1 interconnect]" 11:17:38 msg="Devices changed" devices="[public.1537 public.3212 public.3211 eno1 interconnect]" 11:18:11 msg="Devices changed" devices="[eno1 interconnect]" 11:18:12 msg="Devices changed" devices="[public.1537 public.3212 public.3211 eno1 interconnect]" ``` Each reload leaked a full generation of host datapath programs and their tail-call maps. After 21h uptime: ```bash $ bpftool prog show | grep -cE '^[0-9]+:' 74678 $ bpftool map show | grep -c prog_array 6034 ``` The leak is confined to the per-device path. There are 80 pods on this node, and every per-endpoint program count is exactly 80, while every per-device count is ~5950: ```bash $ bpftool prog show | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="name") print $(i+1)}' \ | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20 6029 tail_no_service_ipv4 <-- leaked 6029 tail_nodeport_rev_dnat_ingress_ipv4 <-- leaked 5949 tail_handle_snat_fwd_ipv4 <-- leaked 5948 tail_handle_ipv4_from_netdev <-- leaked 5948 tail_handle_ipv4_from_host <-- leaked 80 tail_ipv4_to_endpoint <-- correct, == pod count 80 tail_ipv4_ct_ingress <-- correct 80 tail_handle_arp <-- correct ``` Each leaked generation has a distinct program tag, so these are separate compilations that were never released, not multiple references to one program. Reloads frequently abort part-way, because the device disappears while the agent is working on it. Programs are already loaded into the kernel at this point: ```bash level=warn msg="Failed to initialize datapath, retrying later" module=agent.datapath.orchestrator error="failed to retrieve link public.1537 by name: Link not found" ``` ### Impact we got JIT images are allocated from the kernel executable memory region (~1520 MiB on x86_64). The leaked programs filled it: ``` $ grep -E 'bpf_jit|execmem|bpf_prog_pack' /proc/vmallocinfo \ | awk '{c=$3; sub(/\+0x.*/,"",c); s[c]+=$2; n[c]++} \ END {for (k in s) printf "%10.2f MiB %6d %s\n", s[k]/1024/1024, n[k], k}' 987.84 MiB 492 bpf_prog_pack_alloc $ dmesg | grep -c 'execmem: unable to allocate memory' 12466 # in a 2.16-hour window ``` With `CONFIG_BPF_JIT_ALWAYS_ON=y` a failed JIT allocation cannot fall back to the interpreter and returns `-ENOTSUPP` (errno 524). Seccomp filter installation is the most frequent BPF load on a Kubernetes node, so **every container exec fails**: ``` containerd: msg="ExecSync for ... failed" error="... OCI runtime exec failed: unable to init seccomp: error loading seccomp filter into kernel: error loading seccomp filter: errno 524" ``` Exec probes then fail node-wide, pods never become ready, and the node is dead. Only a reboot recovers it. Measured rate: ~3400 leaked programs/hour, so the node dies roughly **one day after every boot** while device churn continues. ### How can we reproduce the issue? On a node with Cilium device auto-detection enabled: ```bash before_p=$(bpftool prog show | grep -cE '^[0-9]+:') before_m=$(bpftool map show | grep -c prog_array) for i in $(seq 1 20); do ip link add leakparent type dummy ip link set leakparent up n=1 for v in 1537 3211 3212; do ip link add link leakparent name leakparent.$v type vlan id $v ip addr add 10.99.$n.1/24 dev leakparent.$v ip link set leakparent.$v up n=$((n+1)) done sleep 5 # let the agent start reloading ip link del leakparent # all three managed devices vanish at once, mid-reload sleep 5 done sleep 30 echo "delta: progs=$(( $(bpftool prog show | grep -cE '^[0-9]+:') - before_p ))" echo "delta: prog_arrays=$(( $(bpftool map show | grep -c prog_array) - before_m ))" ``` Expected: both deltas return to ~0. Actual: they grow monotonically and never drop. A single dummy device added and removed cleanly does **not** leak — the device must disappear while a reload is in flight. ### Cilium Version Client: 1.17.18 Daemon: 1.17.18 Updated new found at: Client: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 Daemon: 1.20.0 450c5314 2026-07-29T08:53:01+02:00 go version go1.26.5 linux/amd64 ### Kernel Version 6.12.92; 7.0.0-22-generic Both by default: CONFIG_BPF_JIT_ALWAYS_ON=y ### Kubernetes Version 1.33 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump From latest cilium 1.20 test: [cilium-sysdump-20260805-141731.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30748085/cilium-sysdump-20260805-141731.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? Related, but both are about *agent restarts* rather than device changes: #46065, #44194. The error reported when the executable memory region is exhausted is misleading and cost us significant debugging time. The agent presents `-ENOTSUPP` as a verifier rejection and prints a stack depth: ``` Verifier error: program tail_handle_snat_fwd_ipv4: load program: operation not supported: stack depth 272 ``` Nothing is wrong with the program or its stack usage. Distinguishing `ENOTSUPP` from an actual verifier rejection would help a lot. ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Pre-flight ahead of 1.20 upgrade doesn't drop CiliumNodeConfig v2alpha1 CRD
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? [Asked first on Slack](https://cilium.slack.com/archives/C1MATJ5U5/p1785758062847279), but another person confirmed experiencing this too. One of the upgrade notes mentioned the upgrade of `CiliumNodeConfig` from `v2alpha1` to `v2`. I checked beforehand: ```sh $ kubectl get ciliumnodeconfigs.v2alpha1.cilium.io --all-namespaces Warning: cilium.io/v2alpha1 CiliumNodeConfig will be deprecated in cilium v1.16; use cilium.io/v2 CiliumNodeConfig No resources found ``` I then installed the preflight check: ```sh $ helm install cilium-preflight oci://quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium --version 1.20.0 \ --namespace kube-system \ --set preflight.enabled=true \ --set agent=false \ --set operator.enabled=false Pulled: quay.io/cilium/charts/cilium:1.20.0 Digest: sha256:8009baed89d99fd84f7ee5cfdbf3a1fae8153452132549833956b6aca8b9d738 NAME: cilium-preflight LAST DEPLOYED: Mon Aug 3 13:32:10 2026 NAMESPACE: kube-system STATUS: deployed REVISION: 1 DESCRIPTION: Install complete TEST SUITE: None NOTES: You have successfully ran the preflight check. Now make sure to check the number of READY pods is the same as the number of running cilium pods. Then make sure the cilium preflight deployment is also marked READY 1/1. If you have an issues please refer to the CNP Validation section in the upgrade guide. Your release version is 1.20.0. For any further help, visit https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.20/gettinghelp ``` Now, I merged my upgrade PR so Flux rolled out the upgrade from 1.19.6 to 1.20.0. However, the operator pods end up in `CrashLoopBackOff` with this error around `CiliumNodeConfig`: ``` time=2026-08-03T11:52:00.976886093Z level=error msg="Start hook failed" module=operator function="apis.createCRDs.func1 (.../k8s/apis/cell.go:64)" error="unable to create CRDs: Unable to create custom resource definition: CustomResourceDefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io \"ciliumnodeconfigs.cilium.io\" is invalid: status.storedVersions[0]: Invalid value: \"v2alpha1\": missing from spec.versions; v2alpha1 was previously a storage version, and must remain in spec.versions until a storage migration ensures no data remains persisted in v2alpha1 and removes v2alpha1 from status.storedVersions" ``` Now the CNP validator didn't return anything: ``` $ kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/cilium-pre-flight-check -c cnp-validator --previous Error from server (BadRequest): previous terminated container "cnp-validator" in pod "cilium-pre-flight-check-f65fdb894-qthmk" not found ``` The `v2alpha1` storage version CRD hasn't been dropped during the upgrade. ### How can we reproduce the issue? I ran an upgrade of Cilium v1.19.6 to v1.20.0 on my homelab cluster. signals.title: Gateway API: Envoy upstream replies from same-node backends lost (RST), nondeterministic across restarts on ARM64
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues Closest matches are #47400 / #46260 / #26584, but those are about **ingress** traffic to L7LB frontends being dropped at TC on specific device types. This issue is different: ingress reaches Envoy fine — it is Envoy's **upstream replies from same-node backends** that are lost, and it is nondeterministic across agent restarts/node reboots. ### Version Reproduced on **v1.19.6** and **v1.20.0** (identical behavior). ### What happened? With Gateway API enabled, a `Gateway` + `HTTPRoute` pointing at a Deployment whose 2 replicas are spread across 2 nodes: requests through the gateway (ClusterIP or NodePort, from host netns or external clients) **alternate 200/503**. The failing half are the requests where per-request load balancing picks the backend pod on the **same node as the serving Envoy**; remote-node backends always work. Hubble for a failing request (Envoy upstream connection to the local backend): ``` 10.244.0.216:52632 (ingress) -> website/website-...:3000 (ID:7959) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN) 10.244.0.216:52632 (host) <- website/website-...:3000 (ID:7959) to-stack FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN, ACK) 10.244.0.216:52632 (host) -> website/website-...:3000 (ID:7959) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: RST) ``` The backend's SYN-ACK goes `to-stack` **without the proxy mark**, the kernel finds no ordinary socket for the transparent-bound tuple and answers RST. `cilium-dbg monitor --type drop` shows nothing for these flows. Control-plane state is consistent the whole time: - `cilium-dbg shell -- db/show services` → `ProxyRedirect=<port> (ports: [80])` present - `cilium-dbg shell -- db/show envoy-resources` → all `Done`, no errors - `cilium-dbg service list` → ClusterIP shows `1 => 127.0.0.1:<proxyPort>/TCP (active)` - `CILIUM_PRE_mangle` TPROXY rule matches the current proxy port - Identical behavior with `bpf.tproxy=true` and `false` **Nondeterminism:** after certain agent restarts the same configuration served 8/8 *including* local backends for a few hours, then regressed to alternating after subsequent node reboots with zero config change. Health appears to depend on datapath programming order, suggesting a race. ### Eliminated during bisection - Gateway API CRD skew — fails with correctly pinned v1.3.0 (on 1.19.6) and v1.6.1 (on 1.20.0) - Kernel version skew — both nodes aligned to the same kernel build, no change - `devices` contents — fails with `{eth0,wlan0}` and `{eth0}` (transient improvement after the change, regressed after reboots) - `bpf.masquerade` true/false (iptables masquerade), `bpf.tproxy` true/false - AppArmor — zero denials involving cilium/envoy in kernel logs - systemd `MACAddressPolicy=persistent` — override to `none` for veth/vxlan applied, no change - Full `helm uninstall` + reinstall, plus clean reboots of both nodes (fresh bpffs) ### Environment (affected) - 2× Raspberry Pi 5, Ubuntu 26.04, kernel `7.0.0-1010-raspi` (also `1016`, aligned — no difference), arm64 - k3s `v1.35.4+k3s1` (`--flannel-backend=none --disable-network-policy --disable-kube-proxy --disable=servicelb --disable=traefik`) - Cilium via helm: `kubeProxyReplacement=true`, `routingMode=tunnel`, `tunnelProtocol=vxlan`, `ipam.mode=kubernetes`, `devices={eth0}`, `bpf.masquerade=false`, `MTU=1450`, `gatewayAPI.enabled=true`, external Envoy DaemonSet (defaults) - Node also has a second physical NIC (`wlan0`) outside `devices`, default route via it; inter-node traffic on `eth0` (/30) ### Not reproducible on kind (same versions, same values) The identical stack on kind serves local and remote backends 12/12, which is what makes the affected environment interesting. Full comparison recipe: ```bash cat > kind.yaml << 'K' kind: Cluster apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4 networking: {disableDefaultCNI: true, kubeProxyMode: none} nodes: [{role: control-plane}, {role: worker}, {role: worker}] K kind create cluster --config kind.yaml kubectl apply --server-side -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.6.1/experimental-install.yaml helm install cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system --version 1.20.0 \ --set kubeProxyReplacement=true --set k8sServiceHost=kind-control-plane --set k8sServicePort=6443 \ --set ipam.mode=kubernetes --set routingMode=tunnel --set tunnelProtocol=vxlan \ --set "devices={eth0}" --set bpf.masquerade=false --set bpf.tproxy=true \ --set gatewayAPI.enabled=true --set l2announcements.enabled=true --set MTU=1450 # then: Gateway (class cilium) + HTTPRoute -> Deployment pinned to worker1, Service :80 # curl the gateway ClusterIP from worker1 (local case) and worker2 (remote case): both 100% OK on kind ``` On the affected k3s/raspi cluster the same manifests yield the alternating 200/503. ### Anything else? Happy to provide a `cilium sysdump` from the affected cluster, re-run any diagnostics, or test patches — the environment is available and the failure is easy to trigger there. Also happy to try a stock-Ubuntu k3s VM to further separate the k3s axis from the raspi kernel if that helps triage. ### Code of Conduct - [X] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns connectivity test fails on RHEL8.10
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns consistently fails in the kube-proxy-1 configuration (using RHEL8.10 kernel) in both ipv4 and ipv6 flavors, although it appears to succeed in all other configurations and cases it runs in (on newer kernels). It is unclear why this happens. Other L7 tests (to-fqdns, client-egress-l7, client-egress-l7-named-port, client-egress-tls-cni) using pod-to-world scenarios are also disabled on RHEL kernels, see commit message in https://github.com/cilium/cilium/commit/b1d70aace8944805dd634ae80b66a4b2be18016c. Possibly the reason this test fails on RHEL is related to that. Also note that this test, as well as the other L7 tests disabled on RHEL, use fake external targets provisioned in Docker. CI runs in which this failure has occurred are listed [here](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/47921#issuecomment-5282481311). The test is currently disabled on RHEL kernels to make scheduled CI runs usable. This issue tracks the underlying bug. ### How can we reproduce the issue? Re-enable the host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns connectivity test on RHEL and run it in the kube-proxy-1 configuration: ``` kernel: 'rhel8.10' kube-proxy: 'iptables' kpr: 'false' tunnel: 'vxlan' host-fw: 'true' ``` ### Cilium Version main branch ### Kernel Version lvh-image-kind_rhel8.10-20260803.013611_amd64 ### Kubernetes Version 1.36.0 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell Action [host-firewall-egress-to-fqdns/host-to-world:http-to-fake.external.service.cilium-0: cilium-test-1/host-netns-8h6h4 (172.20.0.4) -> fake.external.service.cilium-http (fake.external.service.cilium:80)] ❌ command "curl --silent --fail --show-error --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 10 -4 -w %{local_ip}:%{local_port} -> %{remote_ip}:%{remote_port} = %{response_code}\n --output /dev/null [http://fake.external.service.cilium:80](http://fake.external.service.cilium/)" failed: command failed (pod=cilium-test-1/host-netns-8h6h4, container=host-netns): command terminated with exit code 28 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: NetworkPolicy silently not enforced for pods carrying a label with key `host` (v1.20.0)
signals.text: ## Summary A Kubernetes pod carrying a label whose **key** is `host` has **all NetworkPolicy enforcement silently disabled**. The pod is not isolated and nothing anywhere reports a problem. The label's *value* is irrelevant. This is security-relevant: a workload that happens to use a `host` label (e.g. `host: <nodename>`, a common convention for pinning/labelling probes) silently loses its network isolation while passing every health check. ## Steps to reproduce Two pods that are identical except that one carries an extra `host` label, and two identical NetworkPolicies, each selecting its own pod by its `app` label: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: {name: lblbug} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: {name: p-a, namespace: lblbug, labels: {app: p-a}} spec: containers: - {name: c, image: "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.47", args: ["netexec","--http-port=8080"]} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: {name: p-b, namespace: lblbug, labels: {app: p-b, host: anything}} spec: containers: - {name: c, image: "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.47", args: ["netexec","--http-port=8080"]} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: {name: cli, namespace: lblbug, labels: {app: cli}} spec: containers: - {name: c, image: "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.47", command: ["sleep","infinity"]} --- apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: {name: iso-a, namespace: lblbug} spec: podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: p-a}} policyTypes: [Ingress] ingress: [{from: [{podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: nope}}}]}] --- apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: {name: iso-b, namespace: lblbug} spec: podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: p-b}} policyTypes: [Ingress] ingress: [{from: [{podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: nope}}}]}] ``` Then, from `cli`, reach each target on port 8080. **Expected:** both `p-a` and `p-b` are blocked — each is selected by a policy whose only ingress rule matches a label that exists on nothing. **Actual:** ``` p-a {app: p-a} -> BLOCKED (correct) p-b {app: p-b, host: anything} -> REACHABLE (policy not enforced) ``` ## Evidence `cilium-dbg endpoint list` on the node hosting both pods: ``` ENDPOINT POLICY (ingress) POLICY (egress) IDENTITY LABELS 1867 Enabled Disabled 12065 k8s:app=p-a 977 Disabled Disabled 7085 k8s:app=p-b ``` Everything upstream of enforcement looks correct for `p-b`: * the NetworkPolicy object is accepted; the agent logs `NetworkPolicy successfully added` * `cilium-dbg policy get` renders the rule correctly (`Tier: 200`, `"DefaultDeny": true`, `"Ingress": true`) * `cilium-dbg policy subject-selectors` resolves the rule's subject to **exactly that pod's identity**, `USERS=1` * the endpoint reaches the agent's current policy revision, state `ready`, no failing controllers Only `cilium-dbg statedb` (table `policy-computations`) dissents — and it reports **no error**: ``` Identity=12065 (p-a) IngressPolicyEnabled=true rev=2 ingressPortRules=256 Identity= 7085 (p-b) IngressPolicyEnabled=false rev=2 ingressPortRules=1 Err=null ``` The endpoint's BPF policy map for `p-b` holds a catch-all `Allow Ingress ANY`. ## Scope — only `host` One pod per candidate key, each with its own identical policy, all on the same node and namespace: ``` (no extra label) -> BLOCKED (enforced) host -> REACHABLE ** only failure ** world -> BLOCKED (enforced) health -> BLOCKED (enforced) init -> BLOCKED (enforced) remote-node -> BLOCKED (enforced) kube-apiserver -> BLOCKED (enforced) ``` So it is not reserved words generally — it is `host` specifically. ## Why this is easy to misdiagnose `PolicyEnforcement=always` is **also inert** on such a pod. Since `always` is defined to enforce default-deny on every endpoint irrespective of any rule, its failure reads as a broken cluster rather than a bad label — which is how we originally diagnosed it. It is consistent with the endpoint being treated as host-ish somewhere, given the host endpoint is exempt from policy unless the host firewall is enabled (`Host firewall: Disabled` here). This also means the usual checks all pass: the object exists, the agent logged success, translation is right, and the selector resolves to the right identity. Nothing surfaces the problem except the `policy-computations` table. ## Environment * Cilium **v1.20.0** (`v1.20.0-450c5314`), agent image digest `sha256:383968cd5e8873f7976fa76aa6196045643558f4cc9518a207b9335cb24a0e93` * Kubernetes 1.35.5 and 1.35.7 * Talos Linux v1.13.8, kernel `6.18.42-talos` * `kubeProxyReplacement=false` (kube-proxy retained), `ipam.mode=kubernetes`, routing mode tunnel/VXLAN, host firewall disabled, Hubble on a local socket * Reproduced on two independent clusters: a 10-node cluster (5 control planes) and a separate 5-node cluster (3 control planes) built from scratch ## What I have not tested All observations are on Talos Linux. I have **not** yet tried this on kind/minikube or another distro, so I cannot say whether it is substrate-independent — though nothing about the mechanism looks Talos-specific. Happy to add that if useful. ## Note The [Terminology docs](https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/gettingstarted/terminology/) state that label keys are prefixed with their source (`k8s:role=frontend` vs `reserved:host`) specifically to disambiguate user labels from reserved ones, which suggests a pod's `k8s:host=x` should never be conflated with the `reserved:host` identity. I could not find an existing issue or any documented restriction on using `host` as a pod label key.

signals.title: Gateway API: 503 connection timeout for same-node backends with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? Gateway API with L2 announcements and VXLAN tunnel mode produces 503 "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout" for **all backend pods running on the same node that holds the L2 VIP lease**. Backend pods on other nodes work perfectly. The pattern is deterministic and follows the L2 lease holder: - When `node-a` holds the lease: all backends on `node-a` return 503, all backends on other nodes return 200 - When the lease moves (e.g. after a cilium restart): the failures follow the lease to the new holder node Envoy admin cluster stats confirm the pattern. Cross-node connectivity from regular pods (both with and without hostNetwork) works fine - this is specific to the envoy TPROXY path. `proxy-use-original-source-address` is hardcoded to `true` by the Helm chart when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, and cannot be overridden via Helm values. This might be the root cause: envoy connects to same-node pods using the external client's source IP via TPROXY, and the response packet from the backend pod cannot route back to envoy correctly in VXLAN tunnel mode. **Please note that I did this research with Claude. I haven't tested the workaround yet.** ### How can we reproduce the issue? **Environment:** 3-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi (arm64), Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-1016-raspi **Cluster topology:** - `jarvis` (control-plane): 192.168.10.100, pod CIDR 10.0.1.0/24 - `node-a` (worker): 192.168.10.101, pod CIDR 10.0.2.0/24 - `node-b` (worker): 192.168.10.102, pod CIDR 10.0.0.0/24 **Steps:** 1. Install Cilium with the following Helm values: ```yaml kubeProxyReplacement: true gatewayAPI: enabled: true l2announcements: enabled: true l7Proxy: true bpf: tproxy: true devices: eth0 envoy: enabled: true securityContext: capabilities: envoy: - NET_ADMIN - SYS_ADMIN - NET_BIND_SERVICE keepCapNetBindService: true socketLB: enabled: true hostNamespaceOnly: false operator: replicas: 1 ``` 2. Create a CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool and CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy: ```yaml apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool metadata: name: gateway-lan-pool spec: blocks: - start: 192.168.10.50 stop: 192.168.10.50 --- apiVersion: cilium.io/v2alpha1 kind: CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy metadata: name: l2-announcement spec: interfaces: - ^eth0 loadBalancerIPs: true ``` 3. Create a Gateway with multiple HTTPS listeners and HTTPRoutes pointing to services on different nodes 4. Observe that backends on the node holding the L2 lease (check via `kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep cilium-l2announce`) return 503, while backends on other nodes work **Verification commands:** ```bash # Check which node holds the lease kubectl get leases -n kube-system cilium-l2announce-default-cilium-gateway-http-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}' # Check envoy cluster stats (run on the cilium pod of the lease-holding node) kubectl exec -n kube-system <cilium-pod> -- cilium-dbg envoy admin clusters | grep -E "(cx_connect_fail|rq_success|rq_error)" # Test cross-node connectivity from a regular pod (works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> # Test from hostNetwork pod on the lease-holding node (also works fine) kubectl run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{"hostNetwork":true,"nodeName":"<lease-holder>"}}' --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<backend-pod-ip>:<port> ``` Both connectivity tests return 200, proving the issue is specific to the envoy TPROXY path, not general network connectivity. ### Relevant log output Curl response from the gateway for a same-node backend: ``` > GET / HTTP/1.1 > Host: argocd.jarvis-home.dev < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable < content-length: 91 < content-type: text/plain < server: envoy upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection timeout ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for the failing backend (same node as lease holder): ``` argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_connect_fail::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::cx_total::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_active::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_error::14 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::rq_success::0 argocd:argocd-server:80::10.0.2.4:8080::health_flags::healthy ``` Envoy admin cluster stats for a working backend (different node from lease holder): ``` technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_active::6 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_connect_fail::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::cx_total::14 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_active::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_error::0 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::rq_success::67 technitium:technitium-svc:5380::10.0.1.131:5380::health_flags::healthy ``` Relevant cilium-config values: ``` routing-mode: tunnel tunnel-protocol: vxlan proxy-use-original-source-address: "true" enable-bpf-tproxy: "true" external-envoy-proxy: "true" kube-proxy-replacement: "true" gateway-api-hostnetwork-enabled: "false" bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only: "true" ``` ### Workaround Setting `proxy-use-original-source-address: "false"` in the cilium-config ConfigMap and restarting cilium + cilium-envoy DaemonSets resolves the issue. However, this cannot be done via Helm values because the chart hardcodes this to `true` when `kubeProxyReplacement: true`. ### Additional context - The issue was initially observed with technitium (DNS server) being the only pod on the control-plane node. When the L2 lease was on that node, only technitium failed. After a cilium restart moved the lease to a worker node, technitium started working but all worker-node backends broke. - `gatewayAPI.hostNetwork.enabled: true` has no effect when `external-envoy-proxy: true` (Cilium 1.20 default) - no dedicated gateway pods are created. - Related issues with similar symptoms but different root causes: #42325, #35559, #36004, #32592 ### Cilium Version 1.20.0 ### Kernel Version Linux drone-two 7.0.0-1016-raspi #16-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jul 23 22:56:44 UTC 2026 aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version v1.36.3+k3s1 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump [cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31178210/cilium-sysdump-20260818-144359.zip) ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Gateway API: intermittent fixed ~5.02s stall before request is proxied upstream (v1.19.4, VXLAN, no node encryption)
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? # Gateway API: intermittent fixed ~5.02s stall before request is proxied upstream (v1.19.4, VXLAN, no node encryption) ## Summary Requests through a Gateway API listener intermittently stall for a fixed **~5.02 seconds** before the request is proxied to the backend. The backend never sees the request during the stall. Envoy reports no timeouts, retries, or circuit-breaker events, and there is no 5s value anywhere in the effective Envoy config. No requests are lost — with a client timeout above 5s everything completes successfully. Reproducible across four independent clusters. Rate correlates **inversely** with node count, which we cannot explain. ## Environment - Cilium **v1.19.4**, cilium-envoy **v1.36.6** - Gateway API, `kube-proxy-replacement=true` - `routing-mode=tunnel` (VXLAN), jumbo MTU (`cilium_vxlan` 9001, `cilium_wg0` 8921, physical NIC 9001) - `enable-wireguard=true` with **`NodeEncryption: Disabled`** - Managed Kubernetes on AWS, arm64 (Graviton) nodes; Amazon Linux 2023, kernel `6.12.88-119.157.amzn2023.aarch64` - Gateway fronted by an internal L4 load balancer (instance targets, cross-zone enabled, client-IP preservation on) Relevant cilium-config values (no 5s among them): ``` proxy-connect-timeout: 2 proxy-idle-timeout-seconds: 60 http-stream-idle-timeout: 300 proxy-initial-fetch-timeout: 30 gateway-api-service-externaltrafficpolicy: Cluster ``` Effective Envoy config timeouts (from `/config_dump`): `idle_timeout 60s`, `stream_idle_timeout 300s`, `connect_timeout 2s`, `initial_fetch_timeout 30s`, plus `600s`/`900s` route timeouts. **No 5s value.** ## Symptom Client is a pod in-cluster calling an HTTPS hostname routed to the internal Gateway. `curl` timing on a stalled request: ``` total=5.024006 time_appconnect=0.023203 time_starttransfer=5.023998 code=000 ``` TLS completes normally (~23ms), then nothing for ~5.0s. The stall lands at 5.02s regardless of client timeout: | Client timeout | Result | | --- | --- | | `--max-time 5` | 28/30 | | `--max-time 20` | 28/30, the 2 slow ones at **5.025s** and **5.024s** | | `--max-time 30` | **60/60 complete**, 7 slow | Raising the client timeout does not move where the stall lands, so this is not client impatience. ## The backend never receives the request during the stall Backend has a **single replica**, so the backend node is constant and only the Envoy node varies per request. `tcpdump` in the backend pod's netns, correlated with per-request timings. For a request that stalled from `02:18:48.8` to `02:18:53.9`, the backend received **zero packets** for the whole window — the next SYN to `:8080` arrives at `02:18:53.944`, i.e. only after the stall clears: ``` 02:18:48.764381 In IP <envoy-a>.46017 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.802412 In IP <envoy-b>.42843 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.838080 In IP <envoy-a>.44405 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... 02:18:48.874295 In IP <envoy-c>.32887 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... ... 5 SECOND GAP, nothing to the backend ... 02:18:53.944994 In IP <envoy-d>.45869 > <backend>.8080: Flags [S] ... ``` Largest inter-packet gaps on the backend side were `5.066s` and `5.056s`, matching the stalls. Client-side capture of a stalled vs a succeeding connection — byte-identical until the request, then: | | Success | Stalled | | --- | --- | --- | | request (`len 136`) sent | `39.480903` | `39.519219` | | next activity | `39.492036` (**+11ms**) | `44.518844` (**+5000ms**) | So the request is sent and ACKed at TCP level, but not proxied upstream for ~5s. ## The backend is never slow ``` cluster...<backend>_8080.upstream_rq_time: P0=4ms P50=6.0ms P90=7.1ms P99=9.1ms P100=9.1ms ``` Max upstream request time across 90 requests: **9.1ms**. ## Envoy reports no timeout of any kind Zero on all of: `upstream_rq_timeout`, `upstream_rq_retry`, `upstream_rq_per_try_timeout`, `upstream_cx_connect_timeout`, `upstream_cx_overflow`, `circuit_breakers`. No listener `downstream_cx_overflow`, no `downstream_pre_cx_timeout`, no overload-manager activity. Counters that did move over a 60-request run with 7 stalls: | Counter | Value | | --- | --- | | `upstream_cx_idle_timeout` | 44 | | `upstream_cx_destroy_local` | 44 | | `upstream_cx_total` | 47 | | `upstream_rq_per_cx` | P50=2.0 | | `downstream_cx_delayed_close_timeout` | 2 | | `upstream_rq_pending_total` | 41 → 47 | We initially suspected upstream connection-pool churn from this, but **ruled it out**: another cluster with the *lowest* stall rate (~2%) idle-reaps **100%** of its upstream connections (e.g. 103 requests over 102 connections) versus 94% here. Higher churn, lower stall rate — so aggressive idle-reaping appears to be normal behaviour and is not the mechanism. ## Only via the Gateway | Path | Result | Stalls | | --- | --- | --- | | Internal Gateway | 28/30 at 5s timeout | 2 | | k8s Service (`http://svc:8080`) | **30/30** | **0** | | Direct pod IP | **20/20** | **0** | ## Rates across four clusters (5s client timeout, so these are stall rates) | Cluster | Relative node count | Internal Gateway | External Gateway | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | largest (~4.5x smallest) | ~2% | 0% | | B | ~2.2x smallest | ~6% | 0% | | C | smallest | ~18% | 0% | | D | smallest | ~11% | 0% | Cilium version, cilium-envoy version, cilium-config, Gateway API config, load-balancer and target-group attributes, Envoy coverage, MTU, and pod/service CIDRs are identical across all four. **External** Gateway listeners in the same clusters are unaffected (0%). The inverse correlation with node count is consistent but unexplained. It is not a bad AZ or a bad LB node — pinning each load-balancer IP individually gives a uniform rate (2, 3, 2 stalls out of 25 each). ## Ruled out (with evidence) load-balancer target health · Gateway API config · load-balancer/target-group attributes · BPF rate limiting · connection reuse and idle timeout · ALPN · cilium datapath drops (`cilium-dbg monitor --type drop` captured 0 during a live failure) · Hubble drops · Envoy `no_filter_chain_match` · Envoy protocol errors · listen-queue overflow · node churn/age · Envoy coverage · cilium version/config differences · WireGuard · MTU · CIDR collision · client DNS (`time_namelookup` is 1.5ms on stalled requests; `ndots:5` search-path expansion investigated and excluded) · `wireguard-persistent-keepalive=0s` (stalls persist under continuous back-to-back load, including consecutive stalls) · upstream connection-pool churn (see above) · TCP RSTs observed in-pod (they appear on successful requests too — ordinary client teardown) ## Notes on related issues - #40428 (v1.18 hardcoded 5s `connectTimeout`) — fix shipped in v1.19.0; we are on v1.19.4 and our `connect_timeout` is `2s`, so this is not it. - #32592 — we already run `encryption.enabled: true` + `encryption.type: wireguard`, the workaround reported there, and still stall. That report is hostNetwork + VPC-CNI chaining with 100% cross-node failure; ours is intermittent, no hostNetwork. - #46100 — enabling `encryption.nodeEncryption: true` on one cluster took our stall rate from ~12% to **100%**, matching #46100's conditions (VXLAN + node encryption, NIC MTU 9000, `wg0` 8921, v1.19.3+). We reverted. Note this is a **separate** problem: with node encryption disabled we see **no fragmentation drops at all** (`cilium_ipv4_frag_datagrams` untouched, no `DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND`), yet the ~12% stall persists. ## What would help Any pointer to what, in the Gateway API path, could defer proxying an already-accepted request by a fixed ~5s without incrementing any Envoy timeout counter. We are happy to run further captures or provide a sysdump. ### How can we reproduce the issue? ## Reproduction / methods used Packet capture inside a pod (streaming via `kubectl debug -it` was unreliable for us; write to a file and read via `kubectl logs`): ```bash kubectl -n <ns> debug <pod> --image=nicolaka/netshoot:latest --target=<container> -q -- \ bash -c 'tcpdump -i any -nn -S -tttt "tcp port 443" > /tmp/c.txt & sleep 3; <drive traffic>; kill -INT %1; <analyse>' kubectl -n <ns> logs <pod> -c <debugger-name> ``` Envoy admin stats from a node (no curl in the envoy/agent images): ```bash curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/cilium/envoy/sockets/admin.sock http://localhost/stats ``` The Envoy listener port for a Gateway changes on reconfiguration — read it from `/listeners` rather than hardcoding. ### Cilium Version **Environment** - Cilium `v1.19.4`, cilium-envoy `v1.36.6` - `routing-mode=tunnel` (VXLAN), `kube-proxy-replacement=true` - Managed Kubernetes on AWS, **arm64** (Graviton) nodes - Jumbo frames: physical NIC `9001`, `cilium_vxlan` `9001`, `cilium_wg0` **`8921`** ### Kernel Version - Amazon Linux 2023, kernel `6.12.88-119.157.amzn2023.aarch64` ### Kubernetes Version - Managed Kubernetes 1.35 on AWS, **arm64** (Graviton) nodes ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: Host firewall: policy-selected node is permanently isolated after reboot — host endpoint policy map ends up deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip) or allow-all (runtime label add), never the computed policy
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? Closest match is #25448 ("host firewall drops reply traffic for legitimate connections when policies are first enforced"). This report is a stronger manifestation of what looks like the same enforcement-transition problem: in our setup the drop window is not transient — it is fatal and self-sustaining (node permanently isolated until out-of-band reboot), it reproduces on every cold boot, and it also reproduces on a fully synced agent when audit mode is switched off at runtime. Filing separately because the evidence points at the host endpoint's BPF policy map never receiving the computed allow entries, with three distinct end states depending on the path taken. ## What happened? Environment: Cilium 1.18.6 (kubespray), host firewall enabled, kube-proxy replacement enabled, VXLAN tunnel, WireGuard node encryption, `bpf-datapath-mode: netkit`, CRD identity mode, 61 nodes. A `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy` with `nodeSelector` on worker nodes provides ingress lock-down (fromEntities cluster/remote-node/health/host, SSH/ICMP via CiliumCIDRGroup refs plus literal CIDRs, kubelet/NodePort from cluster). **1. Cold boot of a selected node → permanent isolation.** ~13 s after cilium-agent starts, every packet in and out is dropped as `Policy denied` by `bpf_host.c:865`. The node never recovers: the agent needs the apiserver to finish its sync, and its own egress to the apiserver is what is being dropped. Captured from inside a locked node (systemd unit dumping via crictl exec): - at agent start, `cilium-dbg endpoint list` is still **empty** (host endpoint not created yet) while bpf_host is already attached and enforcing deny-by-default with an empty policy map; - 105 659 `Policy denied` drops in 20 s, 73 018 of them the node's own egress to the apiserver LB: `identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:* -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443`; - at that moment the BPF ipcache is fully populated (8 292 entries) and local CIDR identities for the policy's allowed CIDRs are already allocated — e.g. ICMP from an explicitly allowed CIDR is dropped with its allocated identity (`identity 16777222->unknown`). The policy is computed; its allow entries are just not in the host endpoint policy map. **2. Runtime audit-off flip on a fully synced agent → same isolation.** Boot the node with `policy-audit-mode: true` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig): node comes up healthy, host endpoint reaches `state=ready`, realized policy has all 8 L4 ingress rules, `enforcement=audit-ingress`. Then `cilium-dbg endpoint config <hostep> PolicyAuditMode=Disabled` → "configuration updated successfully" → the node is fully isolated within seconds. The agent log ends abruptly mid incremental `UpdatePolicyMaps` processing with no error line — consistent with the deny default being installed while the allow entries never land. **3. Warm enforcement via label add → policy map silently allow-all.** With the agent fully synced and the node label added at runtime (CCNP starts selecting the node), the endpoint reports `enforcement=ingress`, but `cilium-dbg bpf policy get <hostep>` contains only the wildcard pair (`Allow Ingress ANY` prefix 0 / `Allow Egress ANY` prefix 0) — i.e. no actual enforcement. This is the only transition that leaves the node reachable, and it appears to do so by not programming the policy at all. For contrast, a long-running node whose agent processed the CCNP incrementally while already enforcing has a fully programmed map (per-identity allows, port ranges) — so the policy→map pipeline itself works. So the same policy, same version, produces three different host endpoint policy-map end states depending on the transition path: deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip), allow-all (runtime label add), correct (incremental update on an already-enforcing endpoint). Datapath mode does not appear to matter: a cold boot with `bpf-datapath-mode: veth` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig) locked out identically (caveat: the override's application could not be positively confirmed from inside the locked node). Impact: any reboot of a policy-selected node isolates it permanently; recovery requires out-of-band console/rescue access. 54 nodes affected in our cluster. ## Cilium Version 1.18.6 ## Kernel Version 6.8.0-124-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ## Kubernetes Version v1.33.7 (kubespray) ## Sysdump Not attached (production cluster); can provide targeted captures on request. Full monitor drop capture (17 MB) and repeated boot-time snapshots of `endpoint list` / `bpf policy get` / `bpf ipcache list` from inside a locked node are preserved. ## Relevant log output ``` xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 7, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:39186 -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443 tcp SYN xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 2, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity 16777222->unknown: <allowed-admin-ip> -> <node-ip> icmp EchoRequest ``` Agent start with audit mode (the boot that survives): ``` level=warn msg="PolicyAuditMode is enabled. Network policy will not be enforced." level=info msg="Regenerating restored endpoints" restored=0 level=info msg="Creating host endpoint" ``` ## Anything else? - The reboot lockout window matches #25448's "first enforcement" semantics; unlike #25448 the state is permanent because the dropped traffic includes the agent's own apiserver path (chicken-and-egg). - Feature combination overlaps with #31209 (tunnel + KPR + WireGuard + host firewall). - Nothing relevant found in 1.18.7–1.18.13 changelogs. - Happy to run instrumented builds / additional captures on a dedicated test node. ## Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: l2announcer: leader-election Lease name is a plain namespace+name concatenation, so two Services can end up sharing one Lease
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? L2 announcements derive the per-Service leader-election Lease name by gluing the namespace and the Service name onto a prefix with a hyphen, and a hyphen is legal inside both halves. Two unrelated Services can therefore map onto the same Lease name and end up in one leader election. ```go const leasePrefix = "cilium-l2announce" Name: fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s-%s", leasePrefix, svc.Name.Namespace(), svc.Name.Name()), ``` https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/pkg/l2announcer/l2announcer.go#L847-L860 Namespace `foo` + Service `bar-baz`, and namespace `foo-bar` + Service `baz`, both produce `cilium-l2announce-foo-bar-baz`. There is no sanitization, escaping or hashing anywhere on that path; the only other place the name is touched is the GC scan, which just prefix-matches (`strings.HasPrefix(lease.Name, leasePrefix)`) and does not disambiguate either. Same code on v1.19: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/44d55ea770e38bdf4b3a5f5d8079ab311f5a4911/pkg/l2announcer/l2announcer.go#L820-L826 Expected: one Lease per Service. ### Mechanism ### Impact Needs a hyphen in the right place, so it is not going to be common, but it is silent when it happens and the symptom points at the L2 policy rather than at a name collision. Multi-tenant clusters where namespaces are generated with a prefix (`team-a`, `team-a-staging`) and Service names are equally hyphenated are where I would expect it. ### Suggested fix Use a separator that cannot appear in either half. Neither a namespace (DNS-1123 label) nor a Service name (DNS-1035 label) may contain `.`, and `.` is legal in an object name (DNS-1123 subdomain), so `fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s.%s", leasePrefix, ns, name)` is unambiguous and stays readable in `kubectl get leases`. A hash suffix would also work but costs readability. Either way the name changes on upgrade, which orphans the existing Leases. Those are released on agent shutdown (`ReleaseOnCancel`), which empties the holder identity, and `leaseGC` already deletes prefix-matching Leases with an empty holder, so the old objects should clean themselves up. I have not confirmed that. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Enable L2 announcements and a `CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool`. 2. `kubectl create namespace foo && kubectl create namespace foo-bar` 3. Create Service `bar-baz` of type LoadBalancer in `foo`, and Service `baz` of type LoadBalancer in `foo-bar`. 4. Create `CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy` objects selecting both, with disjoint `nodeSelector`s so the two Services are announced from different nodes. 5. `kubectl get leases -n kube-system | grep cilium-l2announce` shows one Lease named `cilium-l2announce-foo-bar-baz` instead of two. ### Cilium Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Kernel Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Kubernetes Version N/A — found by source inspection, no live cluster involved. ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
